item.title: On the $\omega$-circular $*$-distribution for complex unimodular $\omega$
item.description: arXiv:2610.24443v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a notion of $\omega$-circular $*$-distribution $\mu_{\omega}$, defined in terms of a parameter $\omega \in \mathbb{C}$ with $| \omega |=1$. This $*$-distribution appears as limit law in an algebraic central limit theorem (CLT) for $\omega$-commuting unitaries, and interpolates between the Fermionic setting (at $\omega = -1$) and the Bosonic one (at $\omega = 1$). On a combinatorial level, $\mu_{\omega}$ is described in terms of pair-partitions of sets $\{1, ... ,2n\}$, where one has a total order among the $n$ pairs of the partition and where every pair is assigned a direction, to the effect that one can define the sign of a crossing between two pairs. The main goal of the paper is to study a significant subspace, with "Fock space" flavour, of the $L^2$-space associated to a natural multi-variate version of $\mu_{\omega}$. The inner product on this subspace is defined by a sesquilinear form $\langle \cdot \, , \, \cdot \rangle_{\omega}$ on non-commutative polynomials. We explicitly describe $\langle \cdot \, , \, \cdot \rangle_{\omega}$ in terms of some tractable non-negative definite functions on symmetric groups, and we prove that it is non-degenerate if and only if $\omega$ is not a root of unity.
item.dc:creator: Claus Koestler, Liam McQuay, Alexandru Nica

item.title: Calder\'on Commutators on Quantum Euclidean Spaces and Quantum Tori
item.description: arXiv:2610.24881v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the classical setting, Calder\'on's first commutator theorem states that Lipschitz regularity of the symbol characterizes the $L_2$-boundedness of the first commutators. We show that the formally analogous assertion fails on every quantum Euclidean space $\R^d_\theta$ with $\theta\neq 0$. The same simultaneous failure occurs on $\T_\theta^d$ whenever $\theta$ has an irrational entry. For rational $\theta$, we obtain the optimal logarithmic bound for the corresponding Calder\'on first commutator. We also discuss the connection between Calder\'on's first commutator and the $T1$ theorem, and construct an operator-valued counterexample to Calder\'on's first commutator theorem, which shows that there is no direct analogue of the classical $T1$ theorem in the operator-valued setting. The counterexamples and the optimality argument rely on the construction of sequences of matrices $\mathsf D_n$ and $\mathsf A_n$ such that $\|[\mathsf D_n,\mathsf A_n]\|$ is uniformly bounded, whereas $\|[|\mathsf D_n|,\mathsf A_n]\|$ tends to infinity. This phenomenon reflects the failure of the absolute value function to be operator Lipschitz with respect to the operator norm. The logarithmic estimate, on the other hand, is obtained by combining matrix-valued $T1$ theory with a transference argument.
item.dc:creator: Deyu Chen, Guixiang Hong

item.title: Sharp quantum logarithmic Sobolev inequalities via semigroup interpolation
item.description: arXiv:2610.25180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a semigroup interpolation method for sharp logarithmic Sobolev inequalities using spectral calculus and estimates of $\mathrm{Re}\langle\,Lx,x^2\rangle_2$, where $L$ generates an auxiliary symmetric quantum Markov semigroup. We apply the method to free groups and to crossed products of a finite von Neumann algebra $\mathcal N$ by $\mathbb Z$ or $\mathbb Z_n$, for $n=2$ or $n\ge4$, when the action commutes with the semigroup on $\mathcal N$. In particular, the word-length generators on quantum tori and the Weyl word-length generators on $M_n(\mathbb C)$ satisfy logarithmic Sobolev inequalities with optimal constant $2$.
item.dc:creator: Gan Yao

item.title: Noncommutative $L_p$-Poincar\'{e} inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2610.25277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive $L_p$-Poincar\'{e} inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups on finite von Neumann algebras, from a spectral gap (PI) or from a modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality (MLSI). For $p\ge2$, the corresponding coefficients have optimal order $O(p)$ and $O(\sqrt p)$, respectively. Both estimates follow from Beckner inequalities by integration along semigroups. We also establish a non-tracial extension to quantum Markov semigroups satisfying GNS detailed balance. As a direct byproduct, we apply $L_p$-Poincar\'{e} inequalities to Schatten-valued functions on graphs in order to obtain the Schatten distortion of expanders.
item.dc:creator: Li Gao, Marius Junge, Zhendong Xu, Hao Zhang

item.title: A noncommutative weak $L_1$-estimate for rough singular integrals
item.description: arXiv:2610.25339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish a noncommutative version of Andreas Seeger's weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for singular integral operators with kernels satisfying angular $L\log L$ integrability and an averaged radial Dini condition. The strategy for obtaining the sharp integrability condition involves not only some new estimates of the off-diagonal good and bad functions in Parcet's noncommutative Calder\'on-Zygmund decomposition but also certain essential modifications of Seeger's kernel decomposition and estimates.
item.dc:creator: Guixiang Hong, Liang Wang, Xumin Wang, Bang Xu

item.title: Commutative Counterexamples to Arveson's Hyperrigidity Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.26556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct counterexamples to Arveson's hyperrigidity conjecture for operator systems in commutative $C^*$-algebras. In each example, every irreducible representation of the $C^*$-envelope is a boundary representation, but hyperrigidity fails. The first example is the operator system of continuous affine functions on an infinite-dimensional weighted $\ell^p$ ball. In the second infinite-dimensional example, we start with commuting operators and construct a nontrivial dilation. The final example comes from a compact truncated epigraph of a strictly convex function and yields a finite-dimensional operator system.
item.dc:creator: Boris Bilich, Marcel Scherer

item.title: Reduction of structure groups for noncommutative principal bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.26590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a compact group and let $H \subseteq G$ be a closed subgroup. We study reduction of the structure group for noncommutative principal bundles, modelled by free C${}^*$-dynamical systems in the sense of Ellwood. We first describe how induction from $H$ to $G$ behaves on associated correspondences and their tensor structure. Using reconstruction, this leads to a Tannakian characterization of reduction of the structure group in terms of the associated tensor functor. For normal subgroups, we characterize reduction in terms of central equivariant homomorphisms and derive module- and $K$-theoretic obstructions. We conclude with a noncommutative $O(n)$-example which admits no reduction to $SO(n)$.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Wagner

item.title: Charmenability of twin building lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.23424v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Lambda = \mathcal G_A (\mathbb F_q)$ be a minimal simply connected split Kac-Moody group of compact-hyperbolic type, and set $\Gamma=\Lambda/Z(\Lambda)$. We prove that $\Gamma$ is charfinite when $q\geq 11$, or when its Weyl group is $3$-spherical and $q\geq 4$. Here are a few consequences: the only characters of $\Gamma$ are the trivial and regular characters, every invariant random subgroup is supported on $\{e\}$ and $\Gamma$ and these are the only uniformly recurrent subgroups, and every nontrivial unitary $\Gamma$-representation weakly contains the regular representation. Our approach relies on a recent result due to Caprace and Thom, showing that the topological completions $G_+$ and $G_-$ associated to $\Gamma$ have the Howe-Moore property. We prove a criterion of charmenability for irreducible lattices with trivial amenable radical in products of Howe-Moore groups acting geometrically on proper hyperbolic spaces. The criterion requires the visual boundaries to be Poisson boundaries of suitable random walks and the corresponding lattice actions to be essentially free.
item.dc:creator: Cyril Houdayer, Corentin Le Bars

item.title: Translation-Invariant Pure States with Exotic Half-Chain Factors
item.description: arXiv:2610.24154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct translation-invariant pure quasifree fermionic states on the one-dimensional lattice whose half-chain von Neumann algebras are hyperfinite factors of type $\mathrm{II}_\infty$ or $\mathrm{III}_\lambda$ for any $0<\lambda\leq 1$. Via the Jordan-Wigner-Araki transformation, these yield translation-invariant pure spin-chain states with the same half-chain factors, demonstrating that such factors need not be of type I or III. Each state is the unique ground state of a gapless, translation-invariant parent Hamiltonian with superpolynomially decaying interactions. For any fixed factor type, the interval entanglement entropy can exhibit widely varying growth rates, from arbitrarily slow divergence to nearly power-law growth, showing that entropy scaling does not determine the factor type. In contrast, we prove that gauge-invariant quadratic Hamiltonians with finitely many flavours and exponentially decaying hopping exhibit a dichotomy: their ground states either satisfy an area law with a type I half-chain factor, or have logarithmic entropy growth with a type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor. The counterexample was discovered with AI assistance.
item.dc:creator: Ruizhi Liu, Jinmin Yi

item.title: An Atiyah-Segal homomorphism for approximate representations of infinite groups, and almost multiplicative ucp maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.24252v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Atiyah-Segal homomorphism relates the representation ring of a finite group to the $K$-theory ring of its classifying space. We develop a version of this for infinite groups, but based on a ring of approximate representations rather than representations. We then use known results on the Baum-Connes conjecture to show that our homomorphism is an isomorphism for many groups: this includes all torsion-free amenable groups, and all torsion-free fundamental groups of compact manifolds of dimension at most three. The main motivation is the desire to understand approximate representations using topological tools: as a sample application we give some examples of torsion phenomena in approximate representation theory. The methods of proof are $C^*$-algebraic: the key idea is to relate our Atiyah-Segal type homomorphism to Kasparov's coassembly map. The main step realizes (Hausdorffized) $KK$-theory as approximately multiplicative ucp maps modulo stable approximate unitary equivalence for appropriate $C^*$-algebras. This is in the spirit of the stable uniqueness theorems of Dadarlat-Eilers and Lin, and may be of purely $C^*$-algebraic interest.
item.dc:creator: Rufus Willett

item.title: Noncommutative maximal weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for convolution operators under $L_1$-H\"ormander conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.25761v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for families of scalar convolution operators acting on operator-valued function spaces. A joint $L_1$-H\"ormander condition, together with a maximal strong type estimate at one exponent $1<r\leq\infty$, suffices. The kernels may be complex-valued and need not have uniformly bounded $L_1$ norms. Under a size condition, the result also yields a weak endpoint estimate for all sharp truncation radii of singular kernels. This resolves, for convolution kernels, the problem mentioned in \cite[Remark~5.5]{parcet09pseudo} and recalled in Parcet's recent survey \cite[Remark~1.3]{Parcet2026ICM}. The proof involves not only a simultaneous dyadic representation of the operators but also a noncommutative maximal weak type $(1,1)$ estimates of the resulting dyadic operators. This approach seems entirely new even in the commutative setting. Numerous applications are provided. On the one hand, it yields various maximal inequalities and pointwise convergence results for integrable kernels and dyadic approximations of the identity, monotone $L\log L$ majorants, and Poisson integrals on nilpotent groups and symmetric spaces. On the other hand, via various transference techniques, it implies maximal inequalities for Fourier multipliers, Schur multipliers and double operator integrals, together with bilateral almost uniform convergence of dyadic Fourier summation methods on $L_1$ of group von Neumann algebras.
item.dc:creator: Guixiang Hong, Liang Wang, Xumin Wang, Bang Xu

item.title: A vertex operator algebra for the S-fold realisation of a non-unitary Haagerup--Izumi modular fusion category
item.description: arXiv:2610.26341v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that there exists a strongly rational vertex operator algebra $V_{11}$, proposed by Flohr, whose representation theory $\mathrm{Rep}\,V_{11}\simeq\mathrm{Sem}\otimes\mathcal Z(\sigma_2\mathcal F)$ as braided categories. Here $\mathrm{Sem}$ is the semion category (with the spherical structure in which its generator has dimension $-1$), $\mathcal F$ is Ostrik's twisted Haagerup category and $\sigma_2$ is the Galois automorphism $\zeta_{117}\mapsto\zeta_{117}^2$.
item.dc:creator: David E Evans

item.title: Property RD and boundary representations]{Property RD for $\widetilde A_2$ groups\\and boundary representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.26506v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a boundary representation approach to Rapid Decay property for groups acting on buildings of type $\widetilde A_2$. The central estimate combines a multiplicity argument on the product of Furstenberg boundary with the Riesz--Thorin theorem. For simply transitive actions on vertices, we also establish the polynomial bound conjectured by Ramagge, Robertson and Steger in the vector-radial case. The cubic degree of this bound is optimal. The method also uses multiplicity argument with the Riesz--Thorin theorem but on the single Furstenberg boundary.
item.dc:creator: Adrien Boyer, Thang Nguyen

item.title: From vertex operator superalgebras to graded-local conformal nets and back
item.description: arXiv:2304.14263v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We generalize the Carpi-Kawahigashi-Longo-Weiner correspondence between vertex operator algebras and conformal nets to the case of vertex operator superalgebras and graded-local conformal nets by introducing the notion of strongly graded-local vertex operator superalgebra. Then we apply our machinery to a number of well-known examples including superconformal field theory models. We also prove that all lattice VOSAs are strongly graded-local. Furthermore, we prove strong graded-locality of the super-Moonshine VOSA, whose group of automorphisms preserving the superconformal structure is isomorphic to Conway's largest sporadic simple group, and of the shorter Moonshine VOSA, whose automorphisms group is isomorphic to the direct product of the baby Monster with a cyclic group of order two.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Reviews in Mathematical Physics Vol. 38, No. 08, 2550026 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Sebastiano Carpi, Tiziano Gaudio, Robin Hillier

item.title: On Relative Biexactness of Amalgamated Free Product von Neumann Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2505.19508v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given weakly exact tracial von Neumann algebras $M_{1}, M_{2}$ with a common injective von Neumann subalgebra $B$, we prove that the amalgamated free product $M_{1}\overline{*}_{B}M_{2}$ is biexact relative to $\{M_{1},M_{2}\}$. When $M_1$ and $M_2$ are injective but not necessarily tracial, we further show that $M_{1}\overline{*}_{B}M_{2}$ is biexact relative to the amalgam $B$, and if $B$ is mixing in each of $M_1$ and $M_2$, $M_{1}\overline{*}_{B}M_{2}$ itself is biexact. We also develop a new criterion for upgrading relative biexactness and obtain structural decomposition and subalgebra absorption results for amalgamated free product von Neumann algebras that generalize the group case.
item.dc:creator: Kai Toyosawa, Zhiyuan Yang

item.title: Twisted operator algebras of self-similar groupoid actions on arbitrary graphs
item.description: arXiv:2511.07906v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study self-similar groupoid actions on arbitrary directed graphs together with $\mathbb{T}$-valued twists that exhaust the second cohomology group of the associated Zappa-Sz\'ep product category. We define and analyse the associated universal, reduced, and essential $C^*$-algebras, along with their Toeplitz versions and core subalgebras. In fact, we develop our theory in the more general setting of $L^P$-operator algebras, where $P\subseteq [1,\infty]$ is any non-empty set of parameters. This includes $C^*$-algebras, $L^p$-operator algebras and symmetrised $L^{p,*}$-operator algebras for $p\in [1,\infty]$, as special cases. We use three complementary approaches: twisted inverse semigroups, twisted ample groupoids, and $C^*$-correspondences. We provide, in terms of the self-similar action, general characterisations of topological freeness, minimality, Hausdorffness, finite non-Hausdorffness, effectiveness, and local contractiveness for the associated ample groupoids. We generalise the classical Cuntz--Krieger Uniqueness and Coburn--Toeplitz Uniqueness Theorems for graph $C^*$-algebras to twisted $L^P$-operator algebras of self-similar groupoid actions. We characterise when the natural inclusions are Cartan, give checkable criteria for simplicity and pure infiniteness of the essential algebras, and discuss when the universal and reduced algebras coincide. We also provide conditions that ensure the singular ideals vanish. Using the groupoid model we show that for any $P\subseteq [1,\infty]$, the $L^P$-operator algebra of a contracting self-similar action is simple if and only if the corresponding Steinberg algebra is simple. Using the Toeplitz-Pimsner model, we prove that for the universal groupoid of any self-similar groupoid action on a row-finite graph, the singular $C^*$-algebraic ideal always vanishes.
item.dc:creator: B. K. Kwa\'sniewski, A. Mundey

item.title: Equivalence of categories of bivariant K-theory for C*-algebras over topological spaces via reflection functors
item.description: arXiv:2608.22317v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, for various pairs of topological spaces $X$ and $Y$, we introduce an analogue of the Bern\v{s}te\u{\i}n-Gel'fand-Ponomarev reflection functors between the categories of C*-algebras over $X$ and $Y$. We prove that these functors induce equivalences $\mathfrak{KK}(X)_{\mathrm{loc}} \simeq \mathfrak{KK}(Y)_{\mathrm{loc}}$ between Meyer and Nest's localizing subcategories in Kirchberg's ideal-related KK-theory, and $\mathfrak{E}(X) \simeq \mathfrak{E}(Y)$ between the entire categories in Dadarlat and Meyer's ideal-related E-theory. Both equivalences restrict to the respective bootstrap categories: $\mathcal{B}(X) \simeq \mathcal{B}(Y)$ and $\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{E}}(X) \simeq \mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{E}}(Y)$. Combining these equivalences with a combinatorial argument in quiver representation theory, we obtain the same equivalences for any two finite $T_0$-spaces whose Hasse diagrams are orientations of the same tree. Moreover, we prove a rearrangement property of reflection functors, which yields an analogue of Coxeter functors. Finally, we apply reflection functors to give a conceptual alternative proof of Bentmann and K\"ohler's universal coefficient theorem for filtrated K-theory over finite $T_0$-spaces whose Hasse diagrams are orientations of Dynkin diagrams of type A.
item.dc:creator: Nanami Hashimoto

item.title: Regularity for Subfactors
item.description: arXiv:2609.10118v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study three naturally associated notions of regularity for a unital inclusion of von Neumann algebras $\mathcal{B} \subseteq \mathcal{M}$: regularity, groupoid regularity, and unitary regularity. We first observe that regularity and groupoid regularity are unconditionally equivalent by showing that the standard normaliser and the groupoid normaliser of $\mathcal{B}$ in $\mathcal M$ generate the same linear span. The central question addressed in this work is whether regularity implies unitary regularity. For arbitrary von Neumann subalgebras, we demonstrate that this implication fails dramatically; we construct explicit examples to show that every factor (of type $\mathrm{I}_\infty$, $\mathrm{II}_1$, $\mathrm{II}_\infty$, and $\mathrm{III}$) contains a regular von Neumann subalgebra that is not unitarily regular. In stark contrast, we prove that the behaviour changes completely in the setting of subfactors. For subfactor inclusions across all these types, regularity always implies unitary regularity, and thus all three notions of regularity coincide.
item.dc:creator: Keshab Chandra Bakshi, Indrajit Ghosh

item.title: Single commutators in $C^*$-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2609.14585v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal A$ be a simple unital $C^*$-algebra with real rank zero, nonempty tracial state space $\mathcal T(\mathcal A)$, and strict comparison of projections. We prove that every element $T$ in $\mathcal A$ with $\tau(T)=0$ for all $\tau\in\mathcal T(\mathcal A)$ is a single commutator if one of the following conditions holds: $(1)$ $\mathcal A$ has unique trace; $(2)$ $\mathcal A$ has stable rank one. We also prove that every nonscalar element in a simple unital purely infinite $C^*$-algebra is a single commutator. Applications include UHF algebras, irrational rotation algebras, and Cuntz algebras.
item.dc:creator: Lu Cui, Minghui Ma

item.title: Skew fields of non-commutative meromorphic functions affiliated to finite operator algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.21004v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We embed skew fields of meromorphic functions in several non-commuting variables into the topological $*-$algebra of closed linear operators affiliated to a finite von Neumann algebra, $\mathfrak{M}$, with faithful, normal tracial state, $\tau$. Namely, let $\mathscr{O} _d (r)$, $r \in (0, +\infty]$, denote the rings of formal power series in $d \in \mathbb{N}$ non-commuting variables with "radius of convergence" at least $r$ and let $\Xi \in \mathfrak{M} ^{1\times d}$ be a tuple of row-norm $<r$ with the property that there exist no non-zero trace-class operators $T_1, \cdots, T_d \in \mathscr{B} (L^2 (\mathfrak{M}, \tau))$ obeying $\sum _j [T_j , \Xi _j] =0$. Then the unital homomorphism $\mathscr{O} _d (r) \rightarrow \mathfrak{M}$ defined by the evaluation, $\mathfrak{z} _j \mapsto \Xi _j$, extends to an embedding of the universal skew field of fractions of $\mathscr{O} _d (r)$ into the $*-$algebra of closed operators affiliated to $\mathfrak{M}$. In their $L^2-$homology theory of von Neumann algebras, Connes and Shlyakhtenko defined a certain quantity, $0 \leq \Delta (\Xi) \leq d$, as the Murray-von Neumann co-dimension of the Hilbert module generated by all $d-$tuples of finite rank operators obeying the above commutator condition with $\Xi \in \mathfrak{M} ^{1\times d}$. As demonstrated by Mai, Speicher and Yin, this $\Delta$ measures, in a certain precise sense, the algebraic independence of the components of $\Xi$. Connes-Shlyakhtenko proved that $\Delta$ is an upper bound for Voiculescu's non-microstates free entropy dimension, $\delta ^* (\Xi)$, and remark that it is of interest to determine whether these two quantities are equal. Using non-commutative function theory, we show that this is generally not the case, by constructing a triple of self-adjoint operators, $\Xi = (\Xi_1,\Xi_2,\Xi_3)$, for which this inequality is strict, $\delta^*(\Xi) < \Delta(\Xi)$.
item.dc:creator: M\'eric L. Augat, Robert T. W. Martin, Maximilian Tornes, Eli Shamovich

item.title: Applications of $C^*$-Entropy to Representation Growth for Discrete Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.21080v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The topological $1$-bounded entropy $h^\text{top}(C^*(\Gamma))$ of the full group $C^*$-algebra of a finitely generated group $\Gamma$ is given a representation-theoretic interpretation. The implications of Hilbert-Schmidt stability and matricial stability are investigated within this setting, recovering and strengthening a representation growth result of Hadwin and Shulman. The entropy framework is used to prove upper bounds on representation growth for superrigid groups and property (T) groups. This recovers a result of De La Harpe, Robinson, and Valette on the growth rate of the irreducible unitary representations of a property (T) group within the framework of $1$-bounded entropy. A soft proof that $SL_n(\Z)$ admits subexponential representation growth is recorded.
item.dc:creator: Connor MacMahon

item.title: Operator space theory from the maximal viewpoint
item.description: arXiv:2610.21929v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We initiate a theory of ``operator spaces" (in other words subspaces of $C^*$-algebras) with an emphasis on the maximal tensor product. The natural morphisms become the maximally bounded maps instead of the completely bounded ones. With this new looking glass we first examine various issues : lifting and extension properties, local reflexivity, inner derivations, similarity problems.This first part is semi-expository while the second one focuses on the class of von Neumann algebras $M$ such that any completely bounded unital homomorphism on a $C^*$-algebra with values in $M$ is maximally bounded (or equivalently is similar to a $*$-homomorphism via a similarity belonging to $M$). We show that this holds if and only if $M$ is the direct sum of a finite von Neumann algebra and an injective one. This also characterizes the $M$'s such that all completely bounded derivations into $M$ are inner. Our main tool for this is a new characterization of injective von Neumann algebras.
item.dc:creator: Gilles Pisier, Jean Roydor

item.title: Units of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$-equivariant $K$-theory and bundles of UHF-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2410.06947v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider infinite tensor product actions of a finite cyclic group $G$ on the UHF-algebra $D = \text{End}(V)^{\otimes \infty}$ for a finite-dimensional projectively faithful unitary $G$-representation $V$ and determine the equivariant homotopy type of the group $\text{Aut}(D \otimes \mathbb{K})$, where $\mathbb{K}$ are the compact operators on $\ell^2(G) \otimes H_0$ for a separable Hilbert space $H_0$ with $\dim(H_0) = \infty$. We show that this group carries an equivariant infinite loop space structure revealing it as the first space of a naive $G$-spectrum. We identify this spectrum with the positive units $gl_1(KU^D)_+$ of equivariant $KU^D$-theory, which was not possible in the case of circle actions considered by Evans and the second author. Here, $KU^D$ is a $G$-spectrum representing $X \mapsto K_*^G(C(X) \otimes D)$. As a consequence the first group of the cohomology theory associated to $gl_1(KU^D)_+$ classifies equivariant $D \otimes \mathbb{K}$-bundles over finite $G$-CW-complexes.
item.dc:creator: Valerio Bianchi, Ulrich Pennig

item.title: A sharp norm inequality for entanglement-breaking channels
item.description: arXiv:2609.27906v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a channel $\Phi$ on $M_d$ written in the generalised Bloch parameterisation $r \mapsto Ar+c$, we prove that entanglement breaking implies $\|A\|_*^2 + \frac{d(d-1)}{2}\,|c|^2 \;\le\; (d-1)^2 ,$ where $\|\cdot\|_*$ denotes the nuclear norm. Read on the Choi state of the channel, the inequality is an instance of the covariance-matrix criterion of Gittsovich et al.; what is added here is an elementary proof in Holevo form and a complete description of the equality cases. Apart from the constant channel onto a pure state, which shows that the coefficient $d(d-1)/2$ cannot be increased, equality holds exactly for the measure-and-prepare channels with rank-one effects $\alpha_k|e_k\rangle\langle e_k|$ and pure outputs $|\psi_k\rangle\langle\psi_k|$ whose overlaps are an affine image of those of the measurement directions, $|\langle\psi_j|\psi_k\rangle|^2 = P + (1-P)\,(d|\langle e_j|e_k\rangle|^2 - 1)/(d-1)$ for a common $P = \mathrm{Tr}\,\Phi(\mathbf{1}/d)^2$. These include the completely dephasing channel, the re-preparation channel of every rank-one POVM, a one-parameter family interpolating between dephasing and the constant channel, and non-unital non-projective examples already at $d = 2$. The qubit case reads $\|A\|_*^2+|c|^2\le1$ and extends to full rank a rank-two condition of Ruskai. The proof sharpens Ruskai's bound $\|A\|_*\le1$ by retaining the POVM completeness relation $\sum_k f_k=0$, which her argument discards; this recentres $A$ from a second moment into a cross-covariance, and is the entire content of the improvement.
item.dc:creator: Eran Kopel

item.title: On a question of Jones on tracelike vectors, cusp forms, and von Neumann algebras
item.description: arXiv:2609.39904v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using the theory of von Neumann algebras, Vaughan Jones showed abstractly that there is a bridge between holomorphic cusp forms and random matrices. This bridge is supplied by a distinguished function he called a {\it tracelike vector}. He posed the following problem: construct a tracelike vector to make this bridge explicit. We carry out Jones' vision for the full modular group. We construct holomorphic tracelike vectors for every finite-covolume Fuchsian group throughout the permissible Bergman range. For the modular group at the critical parameter $s=13$, we use the resulting unit tracelike vector to assign explicit group coefficients to cusp form multiplication operators, and form positive finite random matrices from a shared Haar-distributed unitary matrix. Almost surely, their normalised traces recover all joint operator moments, first as the matrix size tends to infinity, and then as the group-word cutoff tends to infinity. We also identify the limiting mixed second moment with a series of Petersson norms that involve Maass-Shimura operators of cusp forms. The exact nature of our use of AI is detailed in the introduction.
item.dc:creator: Nikolaos Diamantis, Larry Rolen

item.title: Completely symmetric subspaces of noncommutative $L_p$-spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.18041v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $2<p<\infty$. We prove that every infinite-dimensional closed subspace $F$ of a noncommutative $L_p$-space contains a subspace completely isomorphic to $\ell_p$, $C_p$, $R_p$, or $C_p\cap R_p$ and completely complemented in $F$. This answers the question of Junge and Xu on the existence of completely symmetric basic sequences.
item.dc:creator: Jinghao Huang
